Input reference¶

Use this page to identify the files passed between workflow stages. To write a configuration, use the Reaction-DSL reference, which defines the fields, reaction semantics and structured-filler mappings. The usage guide shows how to generate and consume these files.

File

Provided or generated by

Format and purpose

system.json

User

JSON: reactants, reaction rules and ChemFAST input options

Filler reference

User

PDB: reference geometry, with mappings declared in the DSL

initial.xml

CG preparation

PyGAMD XML: initial particles, coordinates and connectivity

cg_parameters.json

CG parameterization

JSON: bonded and non-bonded CG parameters

run_pygamd_polymerization.py

CG preparation

Python: simulation and reaction-execution protocol

reaction_final.xml

CG simulation

PyGAMD XML: final configuration consumed by FG

reaction_path.txt

CG simulation

Text: one ordered reaction tuple per line, consumed by FG

atomistic.sdf

FG

SDF: AA topology, coordinates and export metadata

system.gro, system.top, *.itp

FF/export

GROMACS coordinates and topology files

Filenames are configurable. Keep the DSL, final XML and ReactionPath from the same construction run together.

Configuration¶

The JSON document combines the reaction-language fields with the following ChemFAST options:

Field

Purpose and format

cg_topology_file

Path to the final PyGAMD XML configuration for FG

reaction_path_file

Path to the matching tuple-per-line ReactionPath text file for FG

box_tensor

Optional initial CG box lengths [Lx, Ly, Lz] in nm for an orthorhombic box

For the low-level build_pygamd_protocol API, omitting box_tensor generates a cubic box from the total system mass and mass_density; the API default is 0.9 g/cm³. The chemfast prepare_cg CLI uses 0.5 g/cm³ as its tutorial-protocol default and accepts --mass-density to override it. Set a box explicitly in the configuration dictionary, or supply a density to the function:

# Explicit initial box (nm):
config["box_tensor"] = [20.0, 20.0, 20.0]
protocol = build_pygamd_protocol(config, output_dir="cg")

# Alternatively, omit box_tensor and set the initial density:
config.pop("box_tensor", None)
protocol = build_pygamd_protocol(config, output_dir="cg", mass_density=0.6)

Import this function from chemfast.cg.pipeline. An explicit box takes precedence over density. During FG, the box is read from the final XML; box_tensor in the JSON is ignored.

The two FG files need not exist during CG preparation. After simulation, pass their actual paths in a copy of the configuration dictionary; the JSON need not be rewritten. For file-based build_pygamd_protocol, relative reference paths resolve against the JSON directory. Direct FG parse_config calls resolve them against work_dir; pass the JSON parent directory or use absolute paths.

Reaction files and correspondence¶

The PyGAMD runner writes reaction_path.txt as one Python tuple literal per line:

('A-B1', 0, 32)
('B1-A', 32, 1)

The first value identifies the reaction; remaining values are zero-based CG node IDs in reactant-slot order. For the first line, node 0 occupies the A slot and node 32 the B1 slot. Lines preserve accepted-event order. Do not sort them or renumber particles independently of the XML. See Workflow for why the final connectivity cannot always replace this record.

The Python reaction engine also provides ReactionPath.to_dict(), a richer event representation containing reaction IDs, steps, participating nodes and sampling metadata. Coupled type changes have separate events linked to the primary event. That representation is not the tuple-per-line input read directly by the current FG parser; do not substitute a JSON event export for reaction_path.txt.

CG configuration: XML¶

The initial and final files use a PyGAMD/GALAMOST-style XML configuration. The final file contains the connectivity built during polymerization. Important sections are:

Section

Contents

configuration

Particle count, dimension and simulation step

box

Box lengths and, where present, tilt factors; use the box convention supported by your workflow

position

One x y z position per particle, in nm in this pipeline

type

One CG type name per particle, consistent with the DSL and parameter JSON

bond

Rows such as A-B1 0 32: bond type and two particle indices

angle

Angle type followed by three particle indices; the middle index is the vertex

mass, charge, image, body

Particle masses, charges, periodic images and rigid-body membership; body = -1 denotes no rigid body

Additional generated sections

Mapping and reaction-state data used by the generated protocol; retain them

Particle indices refer to row order in the per-particle sections, starting at zero. XML stores actual particles and connections; the parameter JSON below stores the force-field terms applied to their types. Both are needed to run the CG simulation. For fields outside this workflow, consult the engine’s XML reference.

CG force-field parameters: JSON¶

get_cgff_parameters writes this file. The CLI and tutorials use cg_parameters.json; low-level API calls may select another filename through the output argument, for example output="cg_ff_parameters.json". The schema is unchanged. Pass the matching file as the parameter argument to the generated runner.

The two top-level objects are bonded and nonbonded. This excerpt shows one bond, one angle and one particle type from the supplied example; it is not a complete runnable parameter set:

{
  "bonded": {
    "A-B1": {
      "ff_type": "CG", "itype": "BOND", "indices": [],
      "params": {"k": 1100.0, "r0": 1.22, "ftype": 1},
      "name": "A-B1", "ff_atom_types": ["A", "B1"]
    },
    "B1-A-B1": {
      "ff_type": "CG", "itype": "ANGLE", "indices": [],
      "params": {"k": 25.0, "r0": 99.8, "ftype": 1},
      "name": "B1-A-B1", "ff_atom_types": ["B1", "A", "B1"]
    }
  },
  "nonbonded": {
    "A": {
      "ff_type": "CG", "ff_atom_type": "A", "bond_type": "",
      "ptype": "A", "params": {"epsilon": 0.663, "sigma": 1.251},
      "element": null, "mass": 1.0, "charge": 0.0,
      "hsp": [19.765, 11.178, 8.281]
    }
  }
}

Download the full supplied parameter example: four particle types (A, B1, B2, C), six bond entries and nine angle entries. It belongs to a different composition from the two-type DSL in the language reference; generate a fresh parameter file from your own DSL instead of using this download interchangeably.

Bonded terms¶

Field

Meaning

Dictionary key / name

Interaction-type name used to associate parameters with CG connections

ff_type

Parameter family, CG

itype

BOND or ANGLE for the current generated PyGAMD runner

ff_atom_types

Ordered CG types; the second type is the angle vertex

indices

Empty for this type-level parameter table; actual particle indices are in the XML

params.ftype

Potential-function code; 1 selects the supported harmonic form

params.k

Harmonic stiffness: CG energy/nm² for bonds, CG energy/rad² for angles

params.r0

Equilibrium bond length in nm for BOND; equilibrium angle in degrees for ANGLE

Thus r0: 1.22 means a 1.22 nm bond, whereas r0: 99.8 means a 99.8-degree angle. PyGAMD’s harmonic-angle setter accepts degrees and converts internally to radians; do not convert the JSON value again. See the engine’s angle convention.

The generator uses conformational sampling to estimate equilibrium geometry; the default stiffnesses are prescribed (bond_k=1100, angle_k=25), not inferred chemical reaction rates. Forward/reverse bond names can both occur, and the runner registers aliases from ff_atom_types; do not independently rename one side of a matching XML/JSON pair. Optional dihedral generation elsewhere in the library does not imply support in this runner, which currently accepts only harmonic bonds and angles.

Non-bonded terms¶

Field

Meaning

Dictionary key / ff_atom_type

CG particle type, e.g. A; must cover the types used by the configuration

params.sigma

LJ size parameter in nm

params.epsilon

LJ well depth in the chosen CG energy scale

hsp

Predicted [dispersion, polar, hydrogen-bonding] components in MPa½

mass, charge

Serialized particle-record values; 1.0 and 0.0 here are CG defaults, not the monomer’s molecular mass or an AA charge prediction

ptype, bond_type, element, ff_type

Shared parameter-record metadata; ptype: "A" is a particle-kind flag, not reactant A

For multi-atom reactants, including multi-atom ions such as TFSI⁻, the current generator predicts HSP components and sets epsilon to their squared magnitude divided by the largest squared magnitude among the included multi-atom types, rounded to three decimals. The largest such type has epsilon = 1. Only monatomic beads (for example [Li+] or [Zn+2]) skip HSP prediction and are excluded from this normalization. A monatomic bead uses twice the element’s RDKit van der Waals radius (converted to nm) for its default sigma and the median of the normalized multi-atom epsilon values for its default epsilon; its serialized hsp is null. Explicit per-reactant sigma and epsilon values override these defaults where supported. An all-monatomic system without an epsilon reference needs explicit ion parameters.

These are approximate, relative construction parameters, not automatically kJ/mol values or validated LJ ion parameters. The elemental vdW radius is not a charge- and coordination-specific ionic radius; in a conventional LJ potential, the energy minimum lies at 2^(1/6) × sigma. Changing the included multi-atom types can change the HSP normalization. The SPE examples’ neutral-default CG mass/charge records do not imply physical lithium or TFSI masses/charges or explicit electrostatics.

The runner uses arithmetic mixing for sigma and geometric mixing for epsilon: sigma_ij = (sigma_i + sigma_j) / 2, epsilon_ij = sqrt(epsilon_i * epsilon_j). It reads these LJ coefficients directly rather than recalculating them from hsp. Editing hsp alone therefore does not change its forces. The runner takes particle masses and charges from the XML, not these JSON metadata fields, and the shown non-bonded force is LJ-only. Rigid filler/site records, including the SPE C/CL records, may use an empirical mean bead size and epsilon = 1 rather than HSP predictions; see the HSP scope.

Object/file

Convention and use

FG internal coordinates and box

Å; CG input lengths are converted from nm

atomistic.sdf

Explicit AA atoms, bonds and coordinates in Å, plus RES_NAMES, RES_NUMS and BOX_TENSOR metadata used by export

system.gro

Coordinates and box in nm, with residue and atom labels; not a complete force-field description

System topology, included parameter files and molecule counts

Molecular connectivity/parameters and shared atom-type definitions

g cm⁻³

sigma in nm and epsilon in kJ mol⁻¹

Elementary charge units

CG temperature/time settings
